songs.note: Ryan Brown documents that an actual Zappa drum part exists for the Interlude, with exactly notated material beside sections where instrumentation is unspecified, and identifies the 9/8 and 4/4 changes. Broader analysis documents sextuplets and 27/16. Split the song by chart coverage first, then let every ghost inherit the evidence level of its own section.
504 on snare and 74 elsewhere. Both halves await per-event adjudication.

LOSES ITS SETTLED LABEL. The evidence proves only that replacing ghost markings with staccato dots was semantically wrong, since duration and dynamic are separate properties. It never proved the 317 original flags were musically correct. Undo the wrong articulation, then adjudicate the 174 snare and 143 non-snare cases separately.

ITS OWN EVIDENCE CLASS. Zappa wrote the piece as a drum solo, so the published material preserves the exact composed rhythm including nested tuplets and irregular subdivisions. Analysis notes Bozzio added hi-hat ticks that were not prescribed, which separates composed attacks from performance additions. Compare all 173 against the written drum score before any decision.
Pure snare, which is a strong prior and not a verdict.
Pure snare, strong prior only.

Ben Wall's 2011 Huddersfield thesis is ON THIS MAC and its Appendix C is a full study score, pages 98 to 132, with a Drum Kit staff. Only the improvised guitar and keyboard solos were omitted. Bar 29 at the head of section [C] carries 7 against 6: drums septuplets against bass sextuplets in the first half, unison semiquavers on beat 3, drums quintuplet against marimba sextuplets on beat 4, under a conducted steady 4/4.
songs.have: Wall thesis pp98-132 on disk, drum staff present
